Harjyot Singh Bhalla Additional Sessions Judge04 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi In The Matter Of: Rajesh Gupta Vs. Delhi Administration (Food Inspector) Ca No. 8720/2016 Rajesh Gupta S/o Shri Ram Khilari Lal Gupta R/o A130, Aruna Park, Shakarpur, Delhi110092 ......Appellant Versus Delhi Administration through Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area Delhi110035 ......Respondent Date of Institution: 03.09.2016 Date of decision : 28.02.2023 Ca No. 8720/2016 1/9 Judgment
texts.facts: (ORAL) 1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose off the appeal filed against the order of conviction dated 02.08.2016 and order on sentence dated 06.08.2016, passed by Ld. ACMMII, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi. 2. The brief facts of the case as per record are that accused was the vendorcumproprietor of M/s Priya Tea Stall, Kiosk No.29, Dr. Rajender Prasad Road, New Delhi01. On 19.07.2004, Food Inspector Sh. Jeet Ram alongwith Field Assistant Sh. Pratap Raj and SDM (LHA) Sh. S.K. Sachdeva visited the said stall and 750 grams of Vanaspati (ready for use) stored in an open tin bearing no label declaration was taken. The said sample was divided into three parts and packed as per Rules. Rajesh Gupta vs . Delhi Administration on 28 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103857142/ 1 Panchanama was prepared. One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst. As per the report of Analyst, sample was not conforming to the standards because it gave negative Baudouin test on mixing of groundnut oil in the ratio 20:80 in terms of standard A.19 Appendix B to the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules. It would be pertinent to note at this stage itself that the Baudouin test is recommended by (x) of the Standards recommended under A.19 of Appendix B to the PFA Rules for detecting the refined sesame (til) oil in the Vanaspati. The relevant portion of the Schedule Standard A.19 is reproduced hereinbelow for ease of reference: A.19... (x) It shall contain raw or refined sesame (til) oil in sufficient quantity so that when the vanaspati is mixed with refined groundnut oil in the proportion of 20:80, the colour produced by the Baudouin test shall not be lighter than 2.0 red unit in a 1cm. cell on a Lovibond scale; 3. The report of the PA reads as follows: 1. BT (vanaspati mixed with refined groundnut oil in the proportion of 20:80) Result Negative. Standard: Not less than 2.0 red units. 4. Similarly, report of the CFL reads as follows: 6. Test for -do- Negative Shall be a) Baudouin on positive Red Dilution 20:80 units 2.0 on sample : Ref. Lovibond Groundnut Oil Tintometer Scale in 1 cm b) Agremone oil -do- Negative cell 5. Therefore, from the aforesaid, it is evident that the PA and CFL both tested the sample for presence of sesame oil and concluded that the same was not detected in consonance with the standard and method prescribed. 6. As the sample had failed to pass the analysis, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint with the court. Accused was summoned for facing trial. 7. Charge was framed against the accused under Section 2 (ia) (a) & (m) of PFA Act; punishable under Section 16 (1) (a) read with Section 7 of the Act of 1954 in these facts and circumstances. 9. In order to prove its case, the prosecution examined following witnesses: PW1 SDM/LHA S.K. Sachdeva PW2 FI Jeet Ram PW3 FA Pratap Raj 10. Prosecution exhibited the following documents: Ex.PW1/A Vendor receipt Ex.PW1/B Notice in Form VI Ex.PW1/C Panchnama Ex.PW1/D Photocopy of NDMC fine receipt Ex.PW1/E Two counterparts of sample alongwith two copies of Form VII Ex.PW1/F Intimation regarding one counterpart deposited with PA Ex.PW1/G PA report Ex.PW1/H Letter to STO Ward no.3 Ex.PW1/J Consent for prosecution Ex.PW1/K Complaint Ex.PW2/A Intimation letter Ex.PW2/B Postal registration receipt copy 11. In his defence, the accused did not lead any evidence. In his Statement under Section 313 Cr.PC, the accused denied all allegations and claimed that he was falsely implicated in the present case.
texts.arguments: Mahavir Prashad (Supra): 3. The trial court basing its opinion on a judgment of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in MCD Vs/ Mehar Singh [1972 FAC 603] has returned a finding that the vanaspati oil which contained til oil imported from a Mediterranean region did not respond to the baudouin test. It would not make any difference whether the Public Analyst was examined or not, as infallibility of the Baudouin test was adjudicated upon by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court and the Hon'ble Punjab & Rajesh Gupta vs .
